strings.app.tagline: Combine your documents into one, then check that nothing was lost, changed or made up
strings.theme.label: Colour theme
strings.settings.heading: Credentials
strings.settings.autosave: Changes save as you make them, row by row. Text you typed but did not save is dropped.
strings.settings.hint: A key is written to this server and never read back. This page only ever learns whether one is set, and its last four characters.
strings.settings.preset.note: The usual address for this provider. Saving a key saves it too.
strings.settings.noendpoint: No endpoint set. Models from this provider cannot be run until there is one.
strings.settings.listed: This endpoint listed {n} model(s); they are in the picker, with no measured figures.
strings.settings.notlisted: This endpoint would not list what it serves. It can still be used: tick "Use a model id not in the table" and type the model id.
strings.settings.catalogue: {n} model(s) from the table can now be picked.
strings.settings.none: Keys cannot be set from this page on this server. It reads them from the environment it was started with.
strings.settings.saved: Saved. The key is on the server and is not readable from here.
strings.settings.endpoint.saved: Endpoint saved. The key stored for this provider was cleared with it.
strings.documents.heading: Documents
strings.documents.hint: Paste or upload the documents you want to combine into one, one per tab.
strings.documents.base.hint: The merged document follows this document's structure. Its title is chosen in step 4, Tuning.
strings.documents.name: Name
strings.documents.count.none: No documents yet. A merge needs at least {min} (up to {max}).
strings.documents.count.one: {n} document added. A merge needs at least {min}.
strings.documents.count.some: {n} documents added. A merge needs at least {min}.
strings.documents.refused.max: This server takes at most {max} documents in one merge and there are already {n}. Remove one before adding another.
strings.documents.refused.min: There must be at least {min} document fields, so this one can't be removed. Add another field first.
strings.documents.dropped.kept: {name} already has text, so nothing was written over it and the files went into empty documents instead.
strings.documents.dropped.notext: Not text, so not loaded: {names}. This tool merges writing; a PDF, an image or an office file would paste as unreadable characters.
strings.documents.dropped.toolarge: Too large, so not loaded: {names}. This server accepts {max} bytes in one submission, documents and settings together.
strings.documents.dropped.overmax: This server takes at most {max} documents in one merge, so these were not loaded: {names}. Merge some of them first, then merge that result with the rest.
strings.controls.heading: Settings
strings.layout.output.run.hint: Shows the run's progress and result once you start a merge.
strings.layout.output.history.hint: Your finished runs will be listed here.
strings.layout.output.empty: Your merged document appears here, checked fact by fact against your originals, so you can see what was kept, lost, changed or made up. Add your documents and press Merge and check.
strings.controls.fidelity: How much the wording may change
strings.controls.depth.estimate: This run: {n} model calls over {docs} documents.
strings.controls.depth.estimate.atleast: This run: at least {n} model calls over {docs} documents; long documents take more.
strings.controls.depth.unmeasured: A benchmark was run, but its figures are not loaded on this server, so how much the cheaper check misses is unmeasured here, which is not the same as nothing. Shown instead: the calls it saves, and what it does not check.
strings.controls.depth.measured.keeps: Where content was lost or contradicted, {depth} caught {caught} of {planted} planted defects and {comparator} {base_caught} of {base_planted}.
strings.controls.depth.measured.caveat: Measured on {date}: one model ({model}), {fixtures} small test cases, {draws} run each. A guide, not a guarantee for your documents.
strings.controls.title: Title
strings.controls.title.policies: "keep-base" keeps the base document's title, or the first title in document order if the base has none. "choose-best" takes the clearest existing title and never writes one. Only "synthesise" may write a new title, and that title is checked against your documents like any other fact.
strings.controls.title.notitle: Nothing is reported when no document has a title and the merge writes none, or when the merged title's words already appear in a document's text. A first line that runs straight into the text is not counted as a title.
strings.depth.full.name: Full
strings.depth.full.explains: Checks both ways: that everything in your documents made it into the merge, and that the merge says nothing your documents do not.
strings.depth.coverage.name: Coverage
strings.depth.coverage.explains: Checks only that everything in your documents made it into the merge. The merge is never read back, so this depth cannot catch invention: anything the merge made up goes unnoticed. It needs fewer model calls.
strings.title.keep-base.explains: The merged document takes the base document's title. Take a different document's title only when the base document has no title at all, or its title is empty. Then take the first non-empty title in document order, and say in the reason that the base document had none.
strings.title.choose-best.explains: The merged document may take any document's title, not only the base document's. Take the one that names the subject most clearly and most completely, and say in the reason what makes it clearer than the others. Where two are equally clear, take the base document's.
strings.title.synthesise.explains: The merged document may take any document's title, or write one that combines them. Prefer an existing title where one already names the subject clearly and completely; taking the base document's title unchanged is always a correct answer at this level and is never penalised.
strings.controls.loss: How much may be left out
strings.controls.loss.hint: The merge may openly leave out up to this share of your documents, and lists every omission. Over it, you still get the merged document, marked for review. The report calls this the declared-loss ceiling.
strings.controls.models.hint: The AI model that writes and checks the merge. Only models you can use here are listed; the scorecard has every model this tool has measured.
strings.models.help.icon.label: What this figure means
strings.models.help.cost: What one merge cost at list prices in this tool's tests. Lower is better. "on plan": it ran on a subscription, which has no price per merge. "free tier": measured on a vendor's free quota. "unmeasured": nobody has run this model through LLossless yet.
strings.models.help.speed: How long one merge took in this tool's tests, in seconds. Lower is better. "unmeasured": nobody has run this model through LLossless yet.
strings.models.help.loss: How many facts from the source documents went missing without the merge saying so, per test (one test is two documents merged). Lower is better; 0 is excellent. "unmeasured": nobody has run this model through LLossless yet.
strings.models.help.deviations_per_pair: How many changes the merge made without flagging them, per test (one test is two documents merged). Lower is better; 0 is excellent. "unmeasured": nobody has run this model through LLossless yet.
strings.models.route.incomparable: A tool here is told the answer format in the prompt rather than having it enforced, and its randomness cannot be fixed, so two runs can give different results. Its figures compare with other tools like it, not with rows that use an API.
strings.models.route.shared: A tool here runs on this server under the server's own login, so every account here shares it: one subscription and one rate limit.
strings.models.route.mark.incomparable.why: This route runs a program on this server. The program is told the answer format in the prompt rather than having it enforced, and its randomness cannot be fixed, so two runs can give different results. Its figures were measured through this same route: compare them with other routes like it, not with rows that use an API.
strings.models.route.caveat.incomparable: A row marked "not directly comparable" runs a program on this server. The program is told the answer format in the prompt rather than having it enforced, and its randomness cannot be fixed, so two runs can give different results. Where such a row shows figures, they were measured through that same route: compare them with other routes like it, not with rows that use an API.
strings.models.route.caveat.shared: A row marked "shared" runs a program on this server with that machine's credentials, so everyone with an account here is on one subscription and one rate limit.
strings.models.route.caveat.cost: A cost cell reading "on plan" is not zero and not missing. A subscription does not tell LLossless how many tokens a merge used, and what you pay is the monthly plan, which cannot be split into a price per merge.
strings.models.route.caveat.freetier: A row marked "measured on the free tier" is still a metered API, as its badge says: with a paid key, the same address bills per token. Only these figures were free. They were measured under the vendor's free daily quota, which is why the cost cell reads "free tier" instead of a price.
strings.models.commands.hint: A tool that runs as a program on this server is set up by whoever runs the server. From a browser you can only switch on the tools the server found on its own machine, under Credentials. The command itself is never sent to a browser.
strings.models.notpriced.note: A self-hosted row has no cost per merge, because its GPU is billed by the minute, not by the token. The cell says "per GPU-minute" instead of showing a zero: it is not free, and it cannot be compared with the per-token prices of hosted rows.
strings.models.split: Use a different model for the checks
strings.models.split.hint: Off, one model does the merge and the checks. On, a second column appears and the two are chosen separately; the report names both.
strings.models.split.commands: A tool on this server cannot do only the checks while the merge goes to an endpoint: one run uses either the tool or an endpoint, never both. To use the tool, pick it in the Use column; it then does the merge and the checks.
strings.models.split.blocked: The checks are set to {name}, a tool on this server, while the merge goes to an endpoint. One run cannot use both, so nothing is sent. Pick another row for the checks, or pick {name} in the Use column.
strings.models.split.blocked.route: Not available while {name} is picked: that tool does the merge and the checks itself, so there is no second model for the checks. To split them, pick a model behind an endpoint in the Use column.
strings.models.pick.use: Use {name} for the merge and the checks
strings.models.bands: Each measured column is banded against a fixed scale, and every band says its word beside the colour. Cost per merge: ${cheap} or less is good, over ${dear} is poor. Seconds per merge: {fast} or less is good, over {slow} is poor. Silent loss: none at all is excellent, one or more per test is poor. Deviations: none at all is excellent, {clean} per test or less is good, {noisy} per test or more is poor. Silent loss and deviations are banded per test and never on the raw count, because these rows were measured over different numbers of tests. A figure nobody measured is left uncoloured.
strings.models.unreachable.blocked: {name} is served by {provider}, and no endpoint is configured for {provider}. Set one on the credentials sheet, or pick a model whose provider has one.
strings.models.custom.toggle: Use a model id not in the table
strings.models.custom.empty: Nothing typed yet, so the table's selection is used.
strings.models.custom.known: {model} is a row in the table, so it goes to that row's endpoint ({provider}) and the choice in "Send it to" does not apply.
strings.models.custom.hint: The id is sent exactly as written to the endpoint chosen in "Send it to"; LLossless does not guess the provider from the name. Only endpoints you have configured are listed. Add one under Credentials.
strings.models.custom.active: The typed id overrides the table: {model} goes to {url}.
strings.models.custom.retired: Warning: {model}, {why}. Use {replacement} instead. The run is not blocked and goes out as typed.
strings.models.custom.window.required: Required: {url} does not report the context window it serves, and LLossless does not guess one.
strings.models.custom.window.optional: Optional: leave it empty to have the window measured, which works on an ollama server; any other server needs it.
strings.models.custom.window.stated: Optional: the table states {tokens} tokens for this model. A figure here replaces it.
strings.models.custom.window.where: The figure is on the vendor's page for this model.
strings.models.custom.window.missing: State the context window for {model}: {url} does not report one, and LLossless does not guess it.
strings.models.custom.window.bad: The context window is a whole number of tokens from {min} to {max}.
strings.models.retired.refused: retired {date}: replaced by {replacement}, and no longer accepted by this version of LLossless
strings.models.catalogue.notes: Not an exhaustive list: the measured rows are every model or subscription route someone actually ran through this tool and recorded, not a curated top-N or a vendor's full lineup. A model missing from this list has not been measured, not been ruled out.
strings.scorecard.heading: Model scorecard
strings.scorecard.hint: Cost, speed and reliability here are measured figures from this tool's own runs, not vendor claims. A figure nobody has measured says so, and sorts last whichever way a column is sorted.
strings.scorecard.sort.hint: Click a column heading to sort by it, and again to reverse. Figures measured on a model the route no longer runs sort after current ones; retired rows and figures nobody measured always sort last.
strings.scorecard.sort.name: Sort by model name.
strings.scorecard.sort.cost: Sort by cost per merge. A row with no measured price - unmeasured, on plan, free tier or per GPU-minute - sorts last either way.
strings.scorecard.sort.speed: Sort by seconds per merge. An unmeasured row sorts last either way.
strings.scorecard.sort.loss: Sort by quality: silent loss per test first, then deviations per test. An unmeasured row sorts last either way.
strings.scorecard.sort.perpair: Sort by deviations per test. An unmeasured row sorts last either way.
strings.models.picker.empty: No AI model is set up yet. Add an API key or an address under Credentials, or type a model id below.
strings.run.heading: Run
strings.run.expect: A merge with {name} took {seconds} on average when it was measured.
strings.status.needdocs: Add at least {min} documents to merge.
strings.status.empty.one: Nothing is in {name} yet. Add its text, or remove it.
strings.status.empty.many: Nothing is in {names} yet. Add their text, or remove them.
strings.status.submitting: Sending the documents. Nothing has been billed yet.
strings.status.running.nodetail: Running. The first model call has not answered yet.
strings.status.done: Done. {advice} The merged document is {chars} characters long.
strings.status.cancelling: Stopping before the next model call. A call already in progress may still be billed.
strings.status.cancelled: The run was cancelled after {n} model call(s). Those calls are billed and cannot be undone.
strings.status.cancelled.queued: The run was cancelled before it started. No model was called.
strings.status.interrupted: The server stopped while this run was in progress, so the run is not complete. It was not restarted, because that would bill its model calls again. Retry starts a new run from the same documents.
strings.status.reconnect: The progress stream dropped and is being resumed from where it stopped.
strings.status.gone: This run has been deleted. Documents and everything derived from them are removed when the retention window passes.
strings.advice.clean: The checks found no problem: every fact in your documents is in the merge, and the merge says nothing they do not. Checked in both directions: {forward} fact(s) from your documents, {reverse} from the merge.
strings.advice.look: The check found statements in the merged document that may be missing or wrong. Please review the items below before you use the document.
strings.advice.record: The document is sound as far as this tool looked; the merge's account of itself is not.
strings.advice.inconclusive: Part of the check did not finish, so this merge has not been cleared. Do not rely on it yet.
strings.advice.notsourced: This run did not look anything up, so it is not a sourced merge. Its corrections come from the model's own knowledge.
strings.results.heading: Result
strings.claims.none: No claims were extracted, so nothing was checked one by one.
strings.section.none.conflicts: The merge recorded no choice between two sources, and no check found a contradiction.
strings.section.none.omitted: Nothing was reported as dropped, and no check found content missing.
strings.section.attributions.note: Each sentence below credits a named source with a statement that source does not contain, while another source contains it word for word. The name was matched to one source by its title or its filename, and no model was asked anything. A sentence the merge copied from a source as written is never listed, and neither is one whose statement no source contains or whose name fits two sources.
strings.section.numbers.note: Each document's decimal style, a point or a comma, is worked out from its own numbers that can only be read one way, then from its language (English writes a point, German a comma), then from most of its numbers; if that ties, it is left open. Listed below: numbers written in the other style, a document whose numbers all use the style its language does not, and numbers such as 17.560 that one style reads as a fraction and the other as thousands. Only a merged value that differs from a settled source value is a fault; every other row is a warning. No number was changed and no model was asked.
strings.section.notchecked: This did not run, so nothing is known either way. An empty list here is not a clean result.
strings.detail.reason: Why it was flagged (the checker's words)
strings.detail.unresolved: The merge recorded the disagreement and chose nothing.
strings.check.title: Title
strings.check.decisions.note: {n} records, written by the merge and not graded by this tool.
strings.check.leaks.note: {n} pieces of the prompt's own example text looked for in the merged document.
strings.check.attributions.note: Merged sentences that credit a named source, held against the text of the source they name. No model is asked.
strings.check.numbers.note: Each document's decimal point or decimal comma, decided from its own numerals and then its language, and every numeral that does not fit it. No model is asked.
strings.check.loss.note: {drops} of {segments} segments openly left out: {achieved}, against a ceiling of {budget}.
strings.check.loss.disabled: The ceiling check was switched off for this run.
strings.check.title.note: Policy {policy}; {n} source documents carried a title.
strings.check.title.noreferent: Policy {policy}; no source document has a title segment, so the policy had nothing to name.
strings.check.order.note: {runs} block(s) over {attributed} segment(s) traced to one source - {shape}. {present} of {total} source headings survive.
strings.check.order.nothing: No merged segment could be attributed to a single source, so nothing can be said about the layout.
strings.order.stapled: each source in one unbroken block
strings.order.unordered: sources in blocks, at least one out of its source order
strings.check.coverage.note: {grounded} of {graded} checked claims found in the merge, {errored} failed with an error, {ungraded} got no answer.
strings.kind.misattributed: Credited to a source that does not state it
strings.kind.other_convention: Written in the other decimal convention
strings.kind.reading_resolved: Open value settled by the merge
strings.numbers.convention: {document}: {convention}, decided {decided}. Votes for a decimal point: {point}; for a decimal comma: {comma}.
strings.numbers.decided.majority: by the majority of its numerals, its language unknown
strings.numbers.decided.none: by nothing: a tie or no vote, and its language unknown
strings.history.heading: Earlier runs on this server
strings.history.hint: Uploads and everything derived from them are deleted when the retention window passes.
strings.error.config: This page could not read the server's configuration, so it cannot offer settings it has not been told about. {detail}
strings.error.merged: The merged document could not be fetched. {detail}
strings.auth.signin.heading: Sign in
strings.auth.signin.hint: This server keeps each account's API keys separate. Yours are yours; the endpoints the operator set up are shared with everybody.
strings.auth.setup.heading: Make the first account
strings.auth.setup.hint: Nothing on this server answers until there is an account. The one made here owns the endpoints everybody shares, and whatever keys this server already holds.
strings.auth.token.hint: This server printed a one-time address when it started. Opening that address fills this in; it works once, and only while there is no account.
strings.accounts.heading: Accounts
strings.accounts.hint: Everyone signed in here can use the endpoints you set up, and can add their own. Their keys are their own; this page never sees them.
strings.accounts.added: {name} can sign in now, with no keys of their own until they set some.
strings.accounts.removed: {name} is gone, and so are the keys they had stored here.
strings.password.heading: Your password
strings.password.hint: Changing it signs this browser out, and every other browser and script signed in as you.
strings.password.changed: Changed. Sign in again with the new one.
strings.settings.notyours: Configured by whoever set this server up, and shared with everybody. Set your own endpoint here to send your runs somewhere else instead.
strings.section.additions.note: The merge declared these statements, and your documents do not contain them. Nothing here has been checked against your documents, because they are the only thing this tool checks against. Each one is the model's own claim, and reviewing it is your job rather than the tool's.
strings.section.additions.sourcing: LLossless did not fetch, resolve or check any source listed here. LLossless itself opens no socket to do it.
strings.section.additions.searched: The model made {n} web request(s) of its own while merging, so a citation here may have been looked up. Which one it belongs to is not recorded, and the statement is still the model's.
strings.section.additions.notsearched: The model made no web request while merging, so every source here is recalled rather than looked up.
strings.section.additions.unmeasured: Whether the model made any web request is unmeasured - this endpoint does not report it - which is not the same as none.
strings.section.additions.corrections: {n} of them correct(s) something a document states. A correction is a departure from your documents, so it is also reported as a finding and it moves the exit code: nothing here can tell a correction from a corruption, and the declaration buys you this row rather than a clean run.
strings.detail.source.none: no source, the model's own knowledge
strings.advice.additions: {n} statement(s) came from outside your documents and could not be checked against them, so for those a clean result means the merge said it was adding them, not that they are true.
strings.advice.retrieval.retrieved: The model retrieved. This run was made at the fidelity level that asks the model to retrieve rather than recall, and {n} of the {m} {calls} that reported a turn count took the turns a retrieval costs. Which statement a retrieval backs is not recorded, and each is still the model's.
strings.advice.retrieval.notretrieved: Nothing was retrieved. This run was made at the fidelity level that asks the model to retrieve rather than recall, and none of its {m} {calls} took the turns a retrieval costs, so every source it names is a recollection, exactly as it would be one level down.
strings.advice.retrieval.unmeasured: Whether anything was retrieved is unmeasured. This run was made at the fidelity level that asks the model to retrieve rather than recall, and {k} of its {calls} reported no turn count, so this page cannot say whether the model looked anything up - which is not the same as saying it did not. Treat every source it names as unchecked.
strings.advice.noinvention: This run checked only that your documents' content survived. Nothing read the merged document back, so nothing here asked whether the merge added anything your documents do not contain: a clean result means content was carried across, not that nothing was invented.
strings.check.additions.note: {n} declared by the merge and not graded by this tool. Only open and sourced, the two highest fidelity levels, permit any.
strings.check.additions.notapplicable: Only open and sourced, the two highest fidelity levels, check for statements added from outside your documents. This run was not made at either.
strings.provenance.effort_single_level: {roles} one level (extended thinking on/off; default kept)
strings.provenance.effort_ignored: {roles} asked for a level this backend cannot carry
strings.cost.floor: A floor, not a total: {unpriced} call(s) could not be priced and {unmeasured} reported no tokens.
strings.cost.unmeasured: Unmeasured: {n} call(s) reported no tokens, so no figure can be derived.
strings.review.note: Each item below needs a decision from you. Select one to jump to it in its own section.
strings.review.addition: Stated on the model's own knowledge
strings.review.addition.cited: Stated with a source the tool did not check
strings.review.decide.conflicts: Decide which version is right, or whether the merged document needs fixing.
strings.review.decide.omitted: Decide whether this belongs back in the merged document.
strings.review.decide.attributions: Decide whether the credit should be corrected.
strings.review.decide.additions: Decide whether to keep this addition.
strings.advice.clean.nothing: There was nothing to check in these documents, so this result proves nothing. Look at the checks below before you rely on it.
strings.advice.clean.forward: The checks found no problem: every fact in your documents is in the merge. {forward} fact(s) from your documents were checked, none in the other direction.
strings.mismatch.label: Possibly not one document
strings.mismatch.text: The merge flagged these documents as possibly not belonging together: "{said}" That is the model's own warning about your inputs, not a fault in the output, and nothing here checks it. If the documents really are unrelated, a clean result only means they were combined faithfully, which may not be what you wanted.
strings.defaults.save: Save these settings as my defaults
strings.defaults.heading: Your defaults
strings.defaults.using: This page starts from your saved settings.
strings.defaults.dropped: No longer available, so the server's default is used instead: {list}.
strings.defaults.unreadable: Your saved defaults could not be read, so the server defaults are used: {detail}
strings.confirm.startover.heading: Clear this and start again?
strings.confirm.startover.text: The documents you pasted, the settings you changed and the result on screen are all cleared. There is no undo. The run itself stays on this server until its retention window passes, and it is still in the list of earlier runs.
strings.confirm.cancel.heading: Cancel this run?
strings.confirm.cancel.text: Calls already made are billed and cannot be undone. Cancelling stops any further calls: the run stops before its next model call, and a call still in progress is abandoned, which the provider may still bill. What ran so far is kept in the report.
strings.confirm.retry.heading: Retry this run?
strings.confirm.retry.text: This starts a new run from the same documents and settings. It runs from the beginning: every model call is made again, and calls may be billed again, including any the stopped run already made. The earlier run stays in the list, and the new one links to it.
strings.confirm.resetdefaults.heading: Reset your settings?
strings.confirm.resetdefaults.text: Your model, checking depth, wording level and tuning choices on this page go back to their defaults. Your saved defaults ("Save these settings as my defaults") are removed too, so this page starts from the server's own defaults next time. There is no undo.
strings.results.judged: Each finding names the document it was judged against. The model is told to use that document alone and to ignore anything it knows from elsewhere, and nothing here can prove it did - so a rationale that reads like general knowledge is one to check against the span it quoted.
strings.banner.heading: This run
strings.commands.heading: Subscription tools on this server
strings.commands.hint: This server looked in its usual install places for the subscription tools it knows by name. Switching one on offers it in the model picker. The browser only ever sees a tool's name, never the command it runs.
strings.commands.missing.hint: This server did not find it in the usual install places. Install it for the user account the server runs as, or add it by hand to the commands file.
strings.commands.owned: The commands file already has a route with this id that was written by hand. It is left exactly as it is: this page switches its own rows on and off and does not edit yours.
strings.commands.retired: The route {ids} was written by an earlier version of this tool and did not say which model it ran, so it has been retired. Switch the model you want on below; nothing you wrote by hand was touched.
strings.commands.enabled: Switched on. It is now a row in the model picker.
strings.commands.disabled: Switched off. It is no longer offered in the picker.
strings.commands.none: Nothing was found: none of the tools this version knows is installed where the server looks. A tool it does not know can be added by hand to the commands file, $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/llossless/commands.json on the server.
strings.commands.unconfigurable: This server was started without a commands file, so a tool cannot be switched on from here. A server started with `llossless serve` always has one.
strings.commands.notyours: Only whoever set this server up can switch one of these on, because a command runs as the server process and is shared by every account here.
strings.commands.pins: Switched on, the tool is told to use {model}, with a context window of {n} tokens. A tool cannot be asked for its window, so this figure is stated, not measured. Change either in the commands file.
strings.retention.window: Runs on this server are deleted {window} after they finish. This one has {left} left.
strings.retention.window.only: Runs on this server are deleted {window} after they finish.
strings.retention.off: Runs on this server are kept until you delete them.
strings.retention.soon: This run has {left} left. Download anything you want to keep.
strings.retention.gone: This run has been deleted, so there is nothing left to download. Documents and everything derived from them are removed when the retention window passes; that window is set with --retention or LLOSSLESS_RETENTION when this server is started.
strings.toolstate.tool-use: The model took more turns on {n} call(s) than a call that retrieves nothing can take, so it used a tool it was granted at least that often. It is a count of turns rather than of fetches, and which statement a retrieval belongs to is not recorded.
strings.toolstate.no-tool-use: No call the model made took more turns than a call that retrieves nothing can take, so it retrieved nothing and every source here is recalled rather than looked up.
strings.toolstate.unmeasured: Whether the model used a tool is unmeasured - this backend reports no turn count - which is not the same as none.
strings.models.route.mark.cli_old: needs Claude Code {needs} or newer (this server has {found})

strings.models.route.name: {model} (subscription)
strings.models.route.caveat.retrieval: A row marked "retrieval" lets the model reach the network. For most rows that is only on a run at the fidelity level that asks for it; at every other level the route answers from what the model already knows. A hand-written command route can grant the tool in its own command line instead, and there it is present at every fidelity level. A Claude Code row runs the CLI in safe mode, so your personal CLAUDE.md, skills, plugins and MCP servers are not loaded, and gives the model only the web tools at that level and no tools at any other unless its own command line grants them. A query or a fetch it makes can carry text from the documents being merged to a third party. LLossless itself opens no socket.
strings.section.additions.sourcednothing: This run was made at the fidelity level that asks the model to retrieve rather than recall, and nothing was retrieved. Every source listed here is therefore a recollection.
strings.fidelity.off.summary: Builds the merge only from sentences your documents already contain, copied exactly. It chooses which ones to keep and in what order.
strings.fidelity.off.buys: Nothing can be reworded into a different meaning: every sentence is one you already had.
strings.fidelity.off.costs: Typos stay, and where two documents disagree, both statements stay. The result can read like a set of quotes rather than one text.
strings.fidelity.low.summary: Also fixes spelling, grammar slips and punctuation. Each sentence stays recognisably the original.
strings.fidelity.low.buys: Reads more cleanly, and no statement changes what it says.
strings.fidelity.low.costs: A corrected sentence is worth a glance against its original. Where two documents disagree, both statements still stay.
strings.fidelity.mid.summary: Also rewrites single sentences for clarity, and may fold a short detail into the sentence it belongs to.
strings.fidelity.mid.buys: Clearer sentences, with small details placed where they belong instead of standing alone.
strings.fidelity.mid.costs: Every folded detail is listed in the report, but the merge now decides where a detail belongs. Where two documents disagree, both statements still stay.
strings.fidelity.high.summary: Rewrites freely, like a careful editor: states a repeated point once, joins facts from both documents into one statement, and settles a disagreement by choosing one value.
strings.fidelity.high.buys: One clear, readable document. The setting most people want.
strings.fidelity.high.costs: Where two documents disagree, the merge picks one value and says which and why, but the choice is its judgement, so check it. Numbers, links, code and version strings are copied exactly at every level.
strings.fidelity.open.summary: Everything high does, and the merge may also correct a fact from what the model knows, or give a range that covers two figures your documents disagree about.
strings.fidelity.open.buys: A document that is wrong about a well-known fact can be fixed rather than copied, and every correction is listed.
strings.fidelity.open.costs: The result can now say things your documents do not. This tool checks only against your documents, so a correction rests on the model's word, and reviewing it is your job. A correction the merge does not list is reported as invented.
strings.fidelity.sourced.summary: Like open, but the model is asked to look facts up on the web instead of recalling them. The report says whether it did.
strings.fidelity.sourced.buys: A correction backed by a published source rather than memory: the difference between a confident wrong answer and a right one.
strings.fidelity.sourced.costs: The model may search the web, so text from your documents can leave this machine in a search or a page request. What it finds is still the model's claim: LLossless checks no source. Where the model cannot use the web, this level is refused rather than answered from memory. Claude Code gets web tools only at this level, unless your own command grants them, and never loads your personal CLAUDE.md, skills, plugins or MCP servers.
strings.section.additions.blindcounter: The endpoint's own web-request counter reported none, which on this backend means it could not see one rather than that none was made: it counts a vendor's server-side tools and a command-line tool runs in the model's own process.
strings.section.difference.legend: `[-...-]` is what the source said and `{+...+}` is what the merge says.
